# Synthetic fixtures

All PDF fixtures are generated by `tools/synthetic_psr.py`. Schools, identifiers,
course examples and grades are invented. They contain no applicant identity.
The title explicitly labels synthetic data; no government logo/signature is used.

- `synthetic_psr.pdf`: two schools, four school/year contexts, page continuation,
  wrapped course name, split credits, proficiency symbols, percent grades,
  unexplained equivalency marker, blank results and one graduation assessment.
- `synthetic_transcript.pdf`: transcript title instead of PSR; must reject.
- `synthetic_unsupported_columns.pdf`: reordered columns; must reject.
- `synthetic_scan.pdf`: no text layer; must reject instead of hallucinating OCR.

Course duration is deliberately absent, as it is in the inspected PSR layout.
The parser must not invent semester/yearly scheduling. M2 will store explicit
supplemental statements/evidence for mixed schedules.

Browser JSON fixtures retain public labels/options and control structure only;
all applicant answers are empty or invented. `mit_coursework_page.json` records
the four required STEM status selectors and two manual narrative fields observed
on the current MIT page. Existing website answers never count as applicant evidence.
The loopback server's native grade route deliberately repeats three element IDs;
it is a selector regression fixture, not a claim that Common App's actual custom
course-edit dialog is supported.
# Grade editor fixture

`grade_dialog_page.json` is a fictional two-course, mixed-scale editor contract.
All school, year, course and grade values are invented. Public control labels
represent the observed Common App widget shape; no applicant values were copied.

`uc_review_state.json` uses public section/action labels and routes with an invented
completion matrix. It contains no applicant answers or identifiers. UC relay tests
model the observed country-selection reset of City, prove a full factual batch
reapplies a known city, and verify unsaved recovery before status navigation.
